% 2026-10-18 (user, second-list 17): parked -- the 250 is the screening stride of the one-off tree search, not a re-estimation of a pre-sample. Was: "the tree pre-sample is re-estimated every 250 intervals."
\item \textit{Notes:} Dates are interval-end dates (ET); Obs.\ and the rolling estimation window $W$ are in the units of each panel. The burn-in, 3{,}125 intervals, is the longest HAR horizon and is applied to each series as built (the closing-interval series, the intraday grid and, for the linear pre-sample, the series of the two intervals of the last hour), so the closing-interval sample starts in 2010 and the pre-sample in 2004. The pooled linear models use $W = \rhdmPooledLinWindow$ intervals (\cmPtFitWin{} trading days); the tree hyperparameters are chosen once, by an Optuna search on the 1998--2002 development sample that fits each candidate on the previous 24{,}000 intervals and scores it on the next 250, stepping forward 250 intervals at a time; the reported forecasts refit every interval. Each validation sample follows a 25-day gap and a \cmPtFitWin-day estimation sample (Section~\ref{sec:rh_exp_samples}). Full trading days: expiration days that are not early-close days. Panel C: the evaluation span holds every trading day on which all rolling forecasts exist (Section~\ref{sec:rh_results_eval}); the straddle economics use its option-data subsample (Section~\ref{sec:rh_econ}).
\end{tablenotes}
